hunks.baseline: When people faced a truth that went far beyond anything they’d expected, their reactions tended to fall into one of two camps.
hunks.sol: When people faced a truth far beyond anything they’d expected, their reactions tended to fall into two camps.

hunks.baseline: They either fell into confusion, unable to understand it, or froze as they grasped the immense shock and weight it carried.
hunks.sol: They either fell into confusion, unable to understand it, or froze as they began to grasp its staggering weight.

hunks.baseline: Confronted with the despairing reality that the master he’d worshiped like a god had abandoned him, the fiend could hear the Grand Mage’s words from a moment ago ringing in his ears again and again.
hunks.sol: Confronted with the crushing reality that the master he’d worshiped like a god had abandoned him, the fiend heard the Grand Mage’s words ringing in his ears again and again.

hunks.baseline: No matter how many times the Blood-Sword Demon Lord turned over the Grand Mage’s words about Jin Taekyung in his mind, he couldn’t understand them.
hunks.sol: No matter how many times the Blood-Sword Demon Lord turned over her words to Jin Taekyung, he couldn’t make sense of them.

hunks.baseline: That was a law of the world he knew well, having walked the Demonic Path all his life.

hunks.baseline: He still didn’t know why he, who had devoted himself to the Lord of Heaven and Dark Heaven, was being discarded. But now that things had come this far, he had no choice but to accept it.

hunks.baseline: And yet, quite apart from that…
hunks.sol: That was one thing. This was another.

hunks.baseline: What on earth did his death—this one-sided execution—have to do with Jin Taekyung getting stronger?
hunks.sol: What did his death, this one-sided execution, have to do with Jin Taekyung growing stronger?

hunks.baseline: But at least one other person here knew the truth the Blood-Sword Demon Lord couldn’t.

hunks.sol: The young man’s lips had gone white, and the muscles of his face had stiffened.

hunks.baseline: He stared at the woman before him with vacant eyes, having even forgotten to breathe. At last, he managed to squeeze out a voice.
hunks.sol: He stared at the woman before him with vacant eyes, forgetting even to breathe. At last, he managed to force out the words.

hunks.baseline: “What are you even… talking about?”
hunks.sol: “What are you even… saying?”

hunks.baseline: This wasn’t a question. It was a denial.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t a question. It was a denial.

hunks.baseline: He couldn’t bear to believe in a reality that couldn’t possibly come true, so he was desperately trying to deny it.
hunks.sol: He didn’t want to believe this impossible reality, so he struggled to deny it.

hunks.baseline: “Do I have to spell out what I mean, right here?”
hunks.sol: “Do I have to tell you what I mean, right here?”

hunks.baseline: The words that turned his ominous suspicion into certainty reached his ears. Jin Taekyung felt his mind turning white.
hunks.sol: The words turned his dreadful suspicion into certainty. Jin Taekyung felt his mind go blank.

hunks.baseline: Only one phrase remained in his empty head.
hunks.sol: Only one phrase remained.

hunks.baseline: For that moment, it was as if the whole world had stopped.
hunks.sol: For a moment, it seemed as though the whole world had stopped.

hunks.baseline: No—maybe I really had mistaken it for that.
If not for my head, which had grown hot as if someone were searing it with a branding iron, while my body remained frozen.
hunks.sol: Maybe I really would have believed it had, if not for my head burning like someone was pressing a hot iron to it while the rest of me stood frozen.

hunks.baseline: I floundered in a storm of confusion.
hunks.sol: I floundered in confusion.

hunks.baseline: Question marks appeared and disappeared, over and over, while reason and emotion lost their bearings and crashed into each other.
hunks.sol: Questions kept surfacing and vanishing. Reason and emotion lost their bearings and crashed into each other.

hunks.baseline: The shock rocking my mind was like—or perhaps greater than—the shock I’d felt when I realized this strange world called Murim wasn’t a game, but another reality.
hunks.sol: The shock was as great as—maybe greater than—what I’d felt when I realized this strange world called Murim wasn’t a game, but another reality.

hunks.baseline: And yet this was undeniably real.
hunks.sol: Yet this was real.

hunks.baseline: I forced down my undying shock with everything I had and squeezed out a voice.
hunks.sol: I fought to suppress my shock and forced out a question.

hunks.baseline: A hoarse, cracked voice, so unfamiliar it might have belonged to someone else, slipped between my lips.
hunks.sol: My voice came out hoarse and cracked, so unfamiliar it might have belonged to someone else.

hunks.baseline: Unlike me, the woman’s answer came back calm and composed.
hunks.sol: The woman’s reply, by contrast, was calm.

hunks.baseline: “Who knows? I’m too insignificant to know everything. But…”
hunks.sol: “Who knows? Someone as insignificant as I am can’t know everything. But…”

hunks.baseline: She had gained power that didn’t belong to this world. Now she stared straight at me. Her eyes and voice were filled with such steadfast faith that it could only be called fanaticism, and they set my senses reeling.
hunks.sol: She had gained power that didn’t belong to this world. Now she stared straight at me, her eyes and voice so full of unwavering faith it could only be called fanaticism. The sight and sound made my senses reel.

hunks.baseline: Like a man under a spell, I muttered the damn name.
hunks.sol: I repeated that damned name like a man under a spell.

hunks.baseline: Ever since the day I’d taken my first steps in Murim, I’d heard it from countless people. And yet I’d never once encountered its true form.
hunks.sol: Ever since I’d taken my first steps in Murim, I’d heard it countless times from countless people. Yet I had never once come face-to-face with the one behind it.

hunks.baseline: The leader of Dark Heaven—or rather, their king and god, the absolute being who sought to defy heaven.
hunks.sol: The leader of Dark Heaven—or rather, their king and god. The absolute being who sought to defy heaven.

hunks.baseline: It was Him.
hunks.sol: Him.

hunks.baseline: Only Him.
hunks.sol: Only him.

hunks.baseline: He knew one of my most closely guarded secrets as clearly as if he were looking at the palm of his hand.
hunks.sol: He knew one of my most closely guarded secrets as plainly as if he were looking at the palm of his hand.

hunks.baseline: But that still didn’t answer the question I’d asked before.
hunks.sol: But that didn’t answer my question.

hunks.baseline: Beneath the white veil covering her face, her red lips curved gently.
hunks.sol: Beneath her white veil, her red lips curved gently.

hunks.baseline: “To be honest, everyone knows that just a few years ago, you weren’t even worth worrying about.”
hunks.sol: “Let’s be honest. Just a few years ago, you weren’t someone we needed to concern ourselves with. Everyone knows that.”

hunks.baseline: “Then that means…”
hunks.sol: “Then…”

hunks.baseline: “It’s simple. We were looking down upon the world, and you shone on your own within it. Bright enough to see clearly, even from far away.”
hunks.sol: “It’s simple. We were watching the whole world, and you began to shine within it. Bright enough to spot even from far away.”

hunks.baseline: “It was fascinating. Watching the spoiled son of a declining frontier family become a Hidden Dragon, then gain the Fire King as his dragon pearl and become a Divine Dragon. And watching you grow at a pace without precedent.”
hunks.sol: “It was fascinating to watch the wastrel of a declining frontier martial family become a Hidden Dragon, then gain the Fire King as his dragon pearl and grow into a Divine Dragon. And to see how fast you grew.”

hunks.baseline: An imugi that had cultivated itself for hundreds of years could become a dragon if it obtained a dragon pearl. But Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been, at best, an earthworm wriggling in muddy water.
hunks.sol: An imugi that had cultivated itself for hundreds of years could become a dragon if it obtained a dragon pearl. But Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been, at best, an earthworm in muddy water.

hunks.baseline: And yet the System had given me boundless opportunities to grow. People had come up with reason after reason for my progress, without me having to offer a single excuse.
hunks.sol: Yet the System had given me boundless opportunities to grow. People had supplied explanation after explanation without my having to make a single excuse.

hunks.baseline: And the teachings of the great martial artist Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King.
hunks.sol: And the teachings of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, a great martial artist.

hunks.baseline: They said all of that had brought me to my current level of strength.
hunks.sol: That, they said, was how I’d reached my current strength.

hunks.sol: So no one suspected a thing.

hunks.sol: No—they *couldn’t* have.

hunks.baseline: Even in this world, with its primitive savagery, there were limits to what people considered possible.
hunks.sol: Even in this world, for all its primitive savagery, there were limits to what people considered possible.

hunks.baseline: But the Grand Mage was telling me now that someone outside their reach—at least, the Lord of Heaven—had been the exception.
hunks.sol: But the Grand Mage was telling me that the Lord of Heaven had been an exception.

hunks.baseline: And she’d revealed another unexpected truth, too.
hunks.sol: And she had revealed something else I hadn’t expected.

hunks.baseline: “We continued to watch under His command, and at last we learned who the Chosen One was.”
hunks.sol: “We kept watching at His command. At last, we learned who the Chosen One was.”

hunks.baseline: My eyes trembled before I could stop them.
hunks.sol: My eyes twitched before I could stop them.

hunks.baseline: “Why? You don’t like the expression? I thought it was rather good.”
hunks.sol: “Why? Don’t you like the name? I thought it was rather good.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t answer the Grand Mage’s question.
hunks.sol: I didn’t answer.

hunks.baseline: A hero of the Great Faction War, who had protected the Nine Provinces from the hundred thousand members of the Demonic Cult.
hunks.sol: A hero of the Great Faction War, who had protected the Nine Provinces from a hundred thousand members of the Demonic Cult.

hunks.baseline: A great martial artist who had always shone brilliantly, wherever he went, and was therefore called one of the Three Saints.
hunks.sol: A great martial artist who had always shone brilliantly wherever she went, earning her a place among the Three Saints.

hunks.baseline: And the reason the Bow Saint had spent decades wandering the land, concealing his identity, was a letter left behind by one person.

hunks.baseline: Above them all, a heaven looking down on everything—the universe, or perhaps Murim itself.
hunks.sol: Above them all stood the heaven that looked down upon everything—the universe, or perhaps Murim itself.

hunks.baseline: The Martial God had left a letter for the Bow Saint.
hunks.sol: The Martial God had left the Bow Saint a letter.

hunks.baseline: He’d told him to find someone who might appear at any time, in any place.
hunks.sol: It told her to find someone who might appear anywhere, at any time.

hunks.baseline: The Chosen One—that is…
hunks.sol: The Chosen One.

hunks.baseline: That only made it harder to understand.
hunks.sol: That made it even harder to understand.

hunks.baseline: I could accept that the Martial God had foreseen my appearance and left the Bow Saint a letter about me.
hunks.sol: I could accept that the Martial God had foreseen my arrival and left the Bow Saint a letter.

hunks.baseline: But why? How?
hunks.sol: But why?

hunks.baseline: “Why would you—or the Lord of Heaven—keep me alive?”
hunks.sol: “Why are you—why is the Lord of Heaven—keeping me alive?”

hunks.baseline: I was the one who’d stood in Dark Heaven’s way more than anyone else.
hunks.sol: I had stood in Dark Heaven’s way more than anyone else.

hunks.baseline: I’d been directly involved in the deaths of four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress, his closest subordinates and limbs. I’d caused him countless other losses, too.
hunks.sol: I’d been directly involved in the deaths of four Demon Lords and the Demon Empress, among his closest subordinates. I’d caused countless other losses, too.

hunks.baseline: From the Lord of Heaven’s perspective, I was someone he could kill a hundred times and still not be satisfied.
hunks.sol: As far as the Lord of Heaven was concerned, he could kill me a hundred times and still not be satisfied.

hunks.baseline: And yet the Grand Mage had said it plainly.
hunks.sol: Yet the Grand Mage had said it plainly.

hunks.baseline: He wanted me to survive, and grow stronger. Stronger than before.
hunks.sol: He wanted me to survive and grow stronger. Stronger than I was now.

hunks.baseline: I had to hear the answer to this question.
hunks.sol: I had to hear the answer.

hunks.baseline: If the Lord of Heaven wanted me alive, then it meant my very existence would one day become a threat to everyone.
hunks.sol: If the Lord of Heaven wanted me alive, then my very existence would someday become a threat to everyone.

hunks.baseline: The shock and trembling were long gone.
hunks.sol: The shock and trembling had passed.

hunks.baseline: At the eyes glimmering dimly through the densely woven white veil, burning with loyalty to their master.
hunks.sol: I fixed my gaze on the Grand Mage. Through her tightly woven white veil, I could make out the gleam of eyes burning with loyalty to their master.

hunks.baseline: At last, her tightly closed red lips moved.
hunks.sol: At last, her red lips parted.

hunks.baseline: “No one in the world would dare presume to guess His deep intentions. But one thing is certain.”
hunks.sol: “No one in the world would dare presume to know His deeper purpose. But one thing is certain.”

hunks.baseline: The corner of her mouth lifted. The expression there was unmistakable scorn.
hunks.sol: The corner of her mouth lifted in unmistakable scorn.

hunks.baseline: “Even if you heard the whole truth, could you resist? You?”
hunks.sol: “Even if you heard the whole truth, could someone like you resist?”

hunks.baseline: As if she were throwing off some cumbersome garment, the Grand Mage cast aside her manners. Smiling, she continued.
hunks.sol: As casually as she might throw off a cumbersome robe, the Grand Mage dropped her manners. Smiling, she went on.

hunks.baseline: “You think it rains because people pray for rain? It doesn’t. The clouds gather, and when the heavens will it, the rain falls. That’s the way of this world. Its natural order.”
hunks.sol: “Do you think rain falls because people pray for it? No. The clouds gather, and it rains when the heavens will it. That’s the way of this world. Its natural order.”

hunks.baseline: A sharp gleam flashed behind her veil. A thick vine crept up my body and tightened around my neck.
hunks.sol: Her eyes flashed behind the veil. A thick vine crept up my body and tightened around my neck.

hunks.baseline: Slowly. And powerfully.
hunks.sol: Slowly. Relentlessly.

hunks.baseline: “If you want to die, I can kill you. But you have to survive, according to His will. You want to live, too. Don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “If you want to die, I can kill you. But you have to survive, just as He wills it. Besides, you want to live, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: My whole body was already bound. As the plant stem slowly tightened around my windpipe, I squeezed out my voice.
hunks.sol: My whole body was already bound. As the vine gradually squeezed my throat, I forced out the words.

hunks.baseline: She’d heard the sincerity in my breathless voice and seen it in my eyes, which were steady despite my labored breathing.
hunks.sol: She had heard the conviction in my breathless voice and seen it in my eyes, steady despite my ragged breathing.

hunks.baseline: Her words trailed off, and the pressure around my neck loosened. I looked at her and gave a short laugh.
hunks.sol: Her words trailed off, and the pressure on my neck eased. I looked at her and gave a short laugh.

hunks.baseline: The vine tightened again, as hard as before.
hunks.sol: The vine tightened again.

hunks.baseline: Even so, I laughed aloud, gasping for breath.
hunks.sol: Even so, I laughed aloud between gasps.

hunks.baseline: Yeah, I was unquestionably the weaker one now.
hunks.sol: Yeah, right now I was unquestionably the weaker one.

hunks.baseline: But in this tug-of-war with our lives on the line, I was going to win.
hunks.sol: But I was going to win this tug-of-war with my life on the line.

hunks.baseline: *Now that it’s come to this, I can do it.*
hunks.sol: *Now that it’s come to this, why not?*

hunks.baseline: I smiled brightly at the Grand Mage, her eyes wide open.
hunks.sol: I smiled brightly at the Grand Mage, whose eyes had gone wide.

hunks.baseline: Then I severed the heart meridians throughout my body with all my strength.
hunks.sol: Then, with all the strength I had, I severed the heart meridians throughout my body.

hunks.baseline: Using that faint power to heal me—the very power she had given me.
hunks.sol: Using the faint healing power she herself had given me.

hunks.baseline: Crack!
hunks.sol: Crunch!
